title: SAP Cloud Connector: qué es y arquitectura
tags: scc, cloud connector, btp, tunnel, on-premise
excerpt: Introducción al SCC y el rol que juega en integraciones BTP ↔ on-premise.
body:
## Concepto
SAP Cloud Connector (SCC) es un componente instalado on-premise que crea un **tunnel seguro** hacia SAP BTP (Business Technology Platform), permitiendo que apps en la nube consuman APIs/servicios del landscape SAP interno sin abrir puertos entrantes en el firewall.

## Analogía
- **VPN clásica**: bidireccional, cualquier tráfico
- **Cloud Connector**: túnel outbound solo (SCC inicia la conexión), granular por 'system' y 'resource'

## Componentes
```
┌────────────┐      encrypted        ┌────────────────┐
│ SAP BTP    │◄─── tunnel (443) ────►│ Cloud Connector│
│ subaccount │      (SCC inicia)     │ (on-premise)   │
│            │                       │                │
└────────────┘                       └───────┬────────┘
                                             │
                              ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐
                              ▼              ▼              ▼
                           SAP ECC       SAP S/4        SAP HANA
                           (RFC/HTTP)    (OData)        (JDBC)
```

## Protocolos soportados
- **HTTP/HTTPS** — REST, OData, SOAP
- **RFC** — SAP-native protocolo
- **LDAP** — auth con directory service
- **TCP/JDBC** — HANA queries directas (limited)
- **Mail** — SMTP/IMAP (raro)

## Ventajas
- **Sin puertos entrantes** — firewall stays cerrado
- **Granular** — solo los recursos autorizados accesibles
- **Auditable** — cada llamada loggeada
- **HA** — configurable con master/shadow instances
- **Principal propagation** — usuario BTP hereda identity en on-premise

## HA (High Availability)
- **Master SCC** — primary, active
- **Shadow SCC** — standby, syncs config del master
- Automatic failover si master down

## Cuándo usar
- App en BTP necesita leer/escribir datos en SAP ECC/S/4 on-premise
- Fiori app en BTP consumiendo OData del backend interno
- Extension app en BTP invocando RFC del ECC
- Reportes cloud pulling data de HANA on-prem

## Cuándo NO usar
- Sistema SAP ya en la nube (BTP-to-BTP no necesita SCC)
- Salidas outbound del backend a internet (usar reverse proxy)
- Full VPN entre datacenters (usar VPN corp regular)

## Requisitos técnicos
- Java 8+ (o JDK bundled)
- Windows Server o Linux (RHEL, SLES, Ubuntu)
- RAM mínimo 4 GB (8 GB recomendado)
- Outbound HTTPS 443 al BTP subaccount
- Certificado SSL válido en el subaccount

## Descargar
https://tools.hana.ondemand.com/#cloud → Cloud Connector.

### Versiones
- **Portable** — no service install, corre desde folder
- **MSI/RPM/DEB** — install as OS service

## Primer setup
1. Descargar + install
2. Acceder al UI: `https://<scc-host>:8443`
3. Login inicial: user=`Administrator`, pass=`manage` (cambiar inmediatamente)
4. Configurar subaccount → connectivity a BTP

## Referencia oficial
https://help.sap.com/docs/connectivity/sap-btp-connectivity-cf/cloud-connector

title: SAP Cloud Connector: instalación en Linux
excerpt: Pasos para instalar Cloud Connector en un servidor Linux (RHEL/SLES/Ubuntu).
body:
## Prerequisites
- Linux 64-bit (RHEL 8+, SLES 15+, Ubuntu 20.04+)
- Java 11+ (o SapMachine 11+ recomendado)
- 4 GB RAM min, 4 vCPU
- Ports:
  - **8443/tcp** — SCC UI
  - **443/tcp outbound** — a BTP
- Root o sudo

## Instalar Java (SapMachine)
```bash
# Descargar SapMachine 17
wget https://github.com/SAP/SapMachine/releases/download/sapmachine-17.0.11/sapmachine-jdk-17.0.11_linux-x64_bin.tar.gz

tar -xzf sapmachine-jdk-17.0.11_linux-x64_bin.tar.gz -C /opt/
export JAVA_HOME=/opt/sapmachine-jdk-17.0.11
export PATH=$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH

java -version
```

## Descargar SCC
1. https://tools.hana.ondemand.com/#cloud
2. **Cloud Connector** → **Linux x86-64 (RPM/DEB)** → download

### RHEL/CentOS/Rocky (RPM)
```bash
sudo rpm -i com.sap.scc-ui-<version>-linux-x64.rpm
```

### Ubuntu/Debian (DEB)
```bash
sudo dpkg -i com.sap.scc-ui-<version>-linux-x64.deb
```

### Portable (tar.gz — no service install)
```bash
tar -xzf sapcc-<version>-linux-x64.tar.gz
cd sapcc-<version>
./go.sh
```

## Config JAVA_HOME para el service
Edit `/opt/sap/scc/config/scc.env`:
```
JAVA_HOME=/opt/sapmachine-jdk-17.0.11
```

## Arrancar service
```bash
sudo systemctl start scc_daemon
sudo systemctl enable scc_daemon
sudo systemctl status scc_daemon
```

## Verificar
```bash
sudo journalctl -u scc_daemon -f
```

### UI
Browser: `https://<scc-host>:8443`

Login inicial:
- User: `Administrator`
- Password: `manage`

**Cambiar password inmediatamente**.

## Firewall
### Local
```bash
sudo firewall-cmd --add-port=8443/tcp --permanent
sudo firewall-cmd --reload
```

### Outbound
Asegurar que port 443 puede salir a `*.hana.ondemand.com`.

## Directorios importantes
- `/opt/sap/scc/` — install root
- `/opt/sap/scc/config/` — config files
- `/opt/sap/scc/log/` — logs
- `/opt/sap/scc/state/` — subaccount state
- `/opt/sap/scc/backups/` — SCC backups

## Update
### RPM
```bash
sudo rpm -U com.sap.scc-ui-<newversion>-linux-x64.rpm
```

### Portable
Descargar new version → replace files → restart service.

### Verificar tras update
UI → **About** → verify version.

## Upgrade en HA
Master/shadow: rolling upgrade:
1. Upgrade shadow first
2. Verify shadow OK
3. Failover master → shadow
4. Upgrade old master
5. Failback

## Uninstall
```bash
sudo rpm -e com.sap.scc-ui
sudo rm -rf /opt/sap/scc  # WARN — destroys config y backups
```

## Logs para debug de install
```bash
tail -f /opt/sap/scc/log/scc_daemon.log
```

title: SAP Cloud Connector: instalación en Windows
excerpt: Pasos para instalar Cloud Connector en Windows Server.
body:
## Requirements
- Windows Server 2019+ (o Windows 10 for dev/test)
- 4 GB RAM, 4 vCPU
- Java 11+ (SapMachine recomendado)
- Admin rights

## Java setup
1. Descargar SapMachine 17 for Windows:
   https://github.com/SAP/SapMachine/releases → `sapmachine-jdk-17.0.11_windows-x64_bin.msi`
2. Install
3. Set `JAVA_HOME` env variable:
   - `System Properties` → **Advanced** → **Environment Variables**
   - Add `JAVA_HOME` = `C:\Program Files\SapMachine\jdk-17.0.11`
   - Add `%JAVA_HOME%\bin` to `PATH`

```powershell
java -version
# openjdk version '17.0.11' 2024-04-16
```

## Descargar SCC
1. https://tools.hana.ondemand.com/#cloud
2. **Cloud Connector** → **Windows x86-64 (MSI)**
3. Save `sapcc-<version>-windows-x64.msi`

## Instalar
1. Right-click MSI → **Install** (as Administrator)
2. Wizard:
   - Install location: default `C:\Program Files\SAP\SAP Cloud Connector\`
   - Java Home: auto-detect (or specify path)
3. Finish

### Command line
```powershell
msiexec /i sapcc-<version>-windows-x64.msi /qn INSTALLDIR='C:\SCC'
```

## Windows service
Installer crea service `SAP Cloud Connector 2.0`:
```powershell
Get-Service 'SAP Cloud Connector*'
Start-Service 'SAP Cloud Connector 2.0'
Set-Service 'SAP Cloud Connector 2.0' -StartupType Automatic
```

## Firewall
Allow port 8443 inbound:
```powershell
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName 'SCC UI' `
    -Direction Inbound -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 8443 -Action Allow
```

## Access UI
`https://<hostname>:8443`

Default:
- User: `Administrator`
- Pass: `manage`

**Change password ASAP** — Settings → **Users**.

## Update
1. Download new MSI
2. Install over existing (uninstall first if minor version)
3. Service auto-restarts

### Rollback
- Uninstall via 'Add/Remove Programs'
- Reinstall older MSI
- Config preserved en `%ProgramData%\SAP\SAP Cloud Connector\`

## Directorios importantes
- `C:\Program Files\SAP\SAP Cloud Connector\` — install
- `C:\ProgramData\SAP\SAP Cloud Connector\` — data + config + logs

## Config JAVA_HOME persist
Installer ya lo hace, verificar en:
```
HKLM\SOFTWARE\SAP\SAP Cloud Connector\Config → JavaHome
```

## Logs
`C:\ProgramData\SAP\SAP Cloud Connector\log\scc_daemon.log`

Tail via PowerShell:
```powershell
Get-Content -Path 'C:\ProgramData\SAP\SAP Cloud Connector\log\scc_daemon.log' -Wait -Tail 20
```

## Backup config
- **UI** → **Configuration** → **Export** — download backup ZIP
- Or copy folder `C:\ProgramData\SAP\SAP Cloud Connector\configuration\`

## Common install issues
### 'Java not found'
- `JAVA_HOME` no defined at system level (user-level insuficiente)
- Reboot after setting env var

### 'Service failed to start'
- Check Event Viewer → **Applications**
- Common: port 8443 already in use
- Fix: change SCC port en `scc.properties` file → restart

### 'Port 8443 conflict'
1. Stop SCC service
2. Edit `C:\Program Files\SAP\SAP Cloud Connector\scc_daemon\scc.properties`
3. Change `port=8443` to another (e.g., 9443)
4. Restart
5. Access UI on new port

title: SAP Cloud Connector: registrar subaccount BTP
excerpt: Conectar SCC a un subaccount de SAP BTP (Cloud Foundry o Kyma).
body:
## Contexto
SCC establece tunnel outbound a BTP. Requires:
- Subaccount ID (GUID)
- Region host (URL)
- Credenciales de user BTP con permisos

## Preparar credentials en BTP
1. BTP cockpit → subaccount destino → **Security → Users**
2. Ver que tenés a un user con role **Cloud Connector Administrator**
3. Or asignárselo

## Ver Region host
- BTP cockpit → **Overview** de subaccount
- **Cloud Foundry Environment** → **API Endpoint**
- Ejemplo: `https://api.cf.eu10.hana.ondemand.com`
- Region host para SCC: `cf.eu10.hana.ondemand.com` (o similar)

### Regions comunes
- **AWS Europe (Frankfurt)**: `cf.eu10.hana.ondemand.com`
- **AWS US East (VA)**: `cf.us10.hana.ondemand.com`
- **Azure Europe (Netherlands)**: `cf.eu20.hana.ondemand.com`
- **AWS Brazil (São Paulo)**: `cf.br10.hana.ondemand.com`

List completa en portal.

## Add subaccount en SCC UI
1. Access SCC UI (`https://<scc-host>:8443`)
2. Login como Administrator
3. **Configuration** → **On Premise** (top-left dropdown) — mostrar subaccounts
4. Click **Add subaccount** button

### Wizard fields
- **Region host**: `cf.eu10.hana.ondemand.com`
- **Subaccount**: subaccount ID (GUID)
- **Display name**: friendly name
- **Description**: opcional
- **User name**: user BTP con Cloud Connector Admin role
- **Password**: password (o certificate)
- **Location ID**: (opcional) tag para multi-SCC scenarios

5. **Save**

## Estado 'Connected'
Después de save → SCC tries tunnel handshake:
- Green icon: connected
- Red icon: error

### Errores frecuentes

#### 'Connection refused' / timeout
- Firewall block outbound port 443
- Proxy required? Configure en **Advanced Settings**
- DNS resolution para `*.hana.ondemand.com`

#### 'Authentication failed'
- Wrong user/password
- User no tiene role 'Cloud Connector Administrator'
- MFA required? Use certificate-based auth

#### 'Region incorrect'
- Subaccount region no matches host provided

## Verificar en BTP cockpit
BTP → subaccount → **Connectivity** → **Cloud Connectors**:
- List de SCCs conectados
- Cada uno con status, version, location ID, last active

## Certificate-based auth (recomendado producción)
Más seguro que password:
1. En BTP → **Security → Trust Configuration** → create trust
2. Generate X.509 cert para SCC
3. En SCC → **Advanced Settings → Use client certificate**
4. Import cert + private key

## Múltiples subaccounts
Un solo SCC puede conectarse a múltiples subaccounts (DEV/QA/PROD):
- **Add subaccount** repetir para cada uno
- Cada uno con sus propios systems + resources
- Isolation total: config de uno no afecta otro

## Location ID
Para multi-region deployments donde 2+ SCCs alimentan mismo subaccount:
- SCC-USA con location ID `US`
- SCC-EUR con location ID `EU`
- App BTP call con header `SAP-Connectivity-SCC-Location_ID: US` → routed al SCC correcto

## Master/Shadow config
At add subaccount:
- **Master**: primary SCC
- **Shadow**: standby (added separately con same subaccount + same location ID)

## Ver tunnel state
SCC UI → subaccount → **Connectivity** → dashboard:
- Tunnel state
- Certificate expiry
- Version peer

## Test connection
**Test** button → SCC sends ping via tunnel → confirms round-trip.

## Config file storage
SCC guarda subaccount config en:
- `/opt/sap/scc/config/scc_config.enc` (Linux)
- `%ProgramData%\SAP\SAP Cloud Connector\configuration\` (Windows)

Encrypted at rest.

## Rotation password / cert
Antes de que password expire en BTP:
- SCC UI → subaccount → **Edit** → new password
- Save → tunnel re-authenticates

## Autorización
- SCC UI: users locales (default `Administrator`) o LDAP
- BTP side: user con **Cloud Connector Administrator** role collection

title: SAP Cloud Connector: exponer sistema on-premise
tags: scc, system, mapping, virtual host, physical
excerpt: Configurar un system (ECC, S/4, HANA) para que BTP pueda accederlo.
body:
## Contexto
Un 'system' en SCC representa un backend on-premise (SAP ECC, S/4HANA, HANA DB, custom API).

Para que BTP hable con él, configuras el mapping.

## Add system
SCC UI → subaccount → **Cloud To On-Premise** → **Access Control** → **Add**.

### Wizard fields
- **Backend type**:
  - ABAP System
  - Application Server Java
  - HANA DB
  - Non-SAP System
- **Protocol**: HTTP, HTTPS, RFC, RFC over SNC, LDAP, TCP
- **Internal host**: hostname/IP del backend (**visible SOLO from SCC — never exposed to BTP**)
- **Internal port**: puerto del backend
- **Virtual host**: nombre 'público' que BTP usa
- **Virtual port**: puerto 'público'
- **Principal Type**: 'None', 'X.509 Cert', 'Kerberos', 'Client Cert'

## Ejemplo config: expose ECC RFC
- Backend type: **ABAP System**
- Protocol: **RFC**
- Internal host: `ecc-prod.empresa.local`
- Internal port: `3300`
- Virtual host: `virtual-ecc`
- Virtual port: `3300`
- Principal type: **None** (uses fixed technical user)

App en BTP conecta a **virtual-ecc:3300** → SCC translates → real backend.

## Ejemplo config: expose OData
- Backend type: **ABAP System**
- Protocol: **HTTPS**
- Internal host: `s4prod.empresa.local`
- Internal port: `443`
- Virtual host: `virtual-s4`
- Virtual port: `443`

## Resource authorization
Por system, definir cuáles resources son accesibles:

Select system → **Resources** tab → **Add**:
- URL path: `/sap/opu/odata/sap/API_BUSINESS_PARTNER/`
- Description: 'Business Partner API'
- Access Policy: **Path And All Sub-Paths**

### Deny by default
Cualquier resource NO listado es rechazado. Whitelist-only approach.

### Wildcards
- `/sap/opu/odata/sap/*` — all OData services
- Con **Access Policy = Path Only**: solo ese exacto
- Con **Access Policy = Path And All Sub-Paths**: incluye subpaths

## Test connection
Select system → **Check Availability** button:
- SCC does ping/handshake al backend
- Green: OK
- Red: unreachable

### Common errors

#### 'Host not found'
- DNS in SCC server incorrect
- Backend IP changed

#### 'Connection refused'
- Firewall between SCC and backend blocks port
- Backend service down

#### 'Certificate not trusted'
- If backend HTTPS with self-signed: import CA in SCC:
  - **Configuration** → **On Premise** → **CA Certificates for X.509 Client** o **Trusted CAs**

## Ver systems en BTP
BTP cockpit → subaccount → **Connectivity** → **Cloud Connectors** → **Exposed Backend Systems**:
- Lista de virtual hosts disponibles
- BTP apps referencean estos names

## Uso desde app BTP
App CF (Cloud Foundry) needs 'destination' apuntando al system:

### Destination config (BTP)
1. Subaccount → **Destinations** → **New Destination**
2. **Name**: `MY_ECC_DEST`
3. **URL**: `http://virtual-s4:443` (virtual host from SCC)
4. **ProxyType**: `OnPremise`
5. **Authentication**: BasicAuthentication + user/pass, o PrincipalPropagation

App code usa destination service SDK → transparent access.

## Ejemplo app Node.js
```javascript
const { getDestination } = require('@sap-cloud-sdk/connectivity');
const dest = await getDestination({ destinationName: 'MY_ECC_DEST' });

// Call OData
const response = await fetch(`${dest.url}/sap/opu/odata/sap/API_BP/A_BusinessPartner`, {
  headers: dest.authTokens[0].http_header
});
```

## Trace de calls
SCC UI → **Log And Trace Files** → HTTP access log:
- Cada call registered
- Filter por virtual host, user, timestamp

## Autorización
- SCC admin: subaccount config
- BTP side: **Destination Administrator** role collection para app users

title: SAP Cloud Connector: principal propagation (identity forwarding)
tags: scc, principal propagation, saml, x.509, sso
excerpt: Propagar identity del user desde BTP al sistema on-premise (no shared account).
body:
## Contexto
Sin principal propagation: BTP app usa 1 técnico account para llamar ECC → todos los users BTP se ven como el mismo user en ECC.

Con principal propagation: cada user BTP se autentica en ECC con **su propia identity**.

### Ventajas
- Audit trail en ECC muestra el user real
- Auth de negocio (S_TCODE, S_TABU) respeta permisos del user
- No shared accounts → security best practice

## Requisitos
1. Trust entre BTP y ECC:
   - BTP subaccount tiene un signing key
   - ECC confía en ese signing key (via STRUST)
2. User en ECC con SAME identifier del BTP user (email match típicamente)
3. Principal propagation habilitado en SCC + destination + backend

## Configurar

### 1. Trust BTP → ECC

#### Descargar cert BTP
- BTP cockpit → subaccount → **Connectivity → Cloud Connectors**
- Select SCC → **Principal Propagation** tab → **Download** cert

#### Importar en ECC via STRUST
1. `STRUST` en ECC
2. Node **SSL Client → SSL Server Standard** → change
3. **Import Certificate** → seleccionar el cert descargado
4. **Add to Certificate List**
5. Save

### 2. Habilitar en SCC subaccount
SCC UI → subaccount → **Cloud To On-Premise** → **Principal Propagation** tab:
- **System Certificate**: seleccionar cert que SCC usa
- Save

### 3. Config en system SCC
Select el system (ECC/S4) → tab **Principal Type**:
- **X.509 Certificate**
- Configure cert dan key

### 4. Config en destination BTP
BTP → subaccount → **Destinations** → edit destination:
- **Authentication**: `PrincipalPropagation`

### 5. Config en backend ECC
Enable X.509 login para ese user:
- `SU01` → user → tab **SNC**
- SNC name: `CN=<user email>,...`

Or batch via **SNC0** (SNC config).

## Testing
1. User loguea a app BTP (SSO SAML → BTP knows the identity)
2. App calls ECC via destination con `PrincipalPropagation`
3. SCC injects X.509 cert with user's SNC name
4. ECC receives, matches SNC name → same user login
5. RFC/OData executed as that user en ECC

### Verify en ECC
`SU53` en ECC del user real (no técnico). Auth checks fail o pass según sus permisos.

## Common issues

### 'User not found'
- SNC name en ECC user master no matches cert Subject
- Adjust en SU01 → SNC tab

### 'Certificate not trusted'
- STRUST doesn't have SCC signing CA
- Re-import cert

### 'Principal propagation not enabled'
- Destination config missing `PrincipalPropagation`
- Or SCC system tab 'Principal Type' set to 'None'

### 'Signature verification failed'
- Cert expired
- Time skew between systems (clock sync)

## Certificate rotation
SCC certs rotate periodically (semestral typical):

### Proceso
1. Notification en SCC UI ~30 días antes
2. Download new cert
3. Import en STRUST (add — don't remove old immediately)
4. Update SCC config
5. Test
6. Después de confirmar OK, remove old cert de STRUST

## Cross-system SSO
Same identity flows across:
- SAP HCM (HR)
- SAP ECC (financials)
- SAP CRM
- Custom Fiori apps en BTP

User inicia sesión una vez en BTP IdP → identity propagates a todos los downstream.

## SAML vs X.509
- **SAML assertions**: cross-Java stack (Java-based Portal)
- **X.509 short-lived certs**: para ABAP RFC/OData (más común hoy)

## Debugging
- SCC log level → DEBUG for `principal propagation`
- Ver `scc_daemon.log` durante the call
- Ver **ICF debug** en ECC (`SICF` trace)

title: SAP Cloud Connector: HA (Master/Shadow)
excerpt: Configuración de alta disponibilidad con Master y Shadow SCC.
body:
## Contexto
SCC solo tiene 1 tunnel activo al subaccount a la vez. **Shadow SCC** replica config del Master y toma over si Master falla.

### Downtime
- Master crash → Shadow detecta en ~30 seg → activates tunnel
- Users apps in BTP may see brief outage

## Requerimientos
- 2 instalaciones separadas de SCC (VM/server distintos)
- Same version en ambos
- Connectivity entre ellos (port 8443 mutuo)
- Same subaccount config

## Setup

### 1. Instalar Master (ya existente)
Asumo tenés SCC configurado con subaccount.

### 2. Instalar Shadow en segundo server
Mismo procedimiento install (Linux/Windows).

### 3. Configurar Shadow como shadow
Shadow UI → **Configuration → High Availability**:
- Role: **Shadow**
- Master host: `master-scc.empresa.local`
- Master port: `8443`
- Client credentials: cert-based recomendado

### 4. Configurar Master
Master UI → **Configuration → High Availability**:
- Role: **Master**
- Allowed shadow: `shadow-scc.empresa.local`

### 5. Sync inicial
Master sends config a Shadow → Shadow ready para failover.

## Estado
En UI de cada uno:
- **Master**: `Master - Tunnel: Connected`
- **Shadow**: `Shadow - Waiting for takeover`

## Ver sync status
Master UI → **Configuration → High Availability** → **Sync History**:
- Timestamps de últimas syncs
- Delta sync (only changes)

## Automatic failover
Si Master pierde tunnel a BTP por más de N segs (configurable):
1. Shadow detects (Master heartbeat missing)
2. Shadow activates tunnel
3. BTP redirects requests to Shadow's tunnel
4. Shadow is now 'temporary master'

At this point:
- Shadow serves traffic
- Original master (if reachable) is in 'passive' state

## Failback manual
Después de resolver issue en Master:
1. Verify Master hardware/network OK
2. UI Shadow → menu **Force Master role back to XXX**
3. Shadow releases tunnel
4. Master re-activates tunnel

### Auto-failback
No automatic. Preferred practice: manual failback en window controlada.

## Considerations

### Bandwidth
Both SCCs need connectivity to BTP + backend. Same network.

### Version match
Both same version. Upgrade:
1. Upgrade Shadow first (no traffic)
2. Verify OK
3. Force failover Master → Shadow
4. Upgrade old Master
5. Failback

### Config drift
Since Master pushes to Shadow, no manual edits en Shadow directly. Always via Master.

### Multiple subaccounts
Master/Shadow relationship applies per subaccount. Puede tenerse:
- SCC-A master for subaccount X, shadow for subaccount Y
- SCC-B shadow for subaccount X, master for subaccount Y

Cross-shadowing (rare pattern).

## Monitoring HA
### From SCC UI
- Master: **High Availability** → last sync, shadow health
- Shadow: same view, plus 'time since last sync'

### From BTP
BTP cockpit → Cloud Connectors:
- If Master fails, entry updates to show Shadow instance

### Alerts
SCC UI → **Configuration → Notifications**:
- Alerts on tunnel state change
- Alerts on HA state change
- Email destination configurable

## Common issues

### Shadow can't sync
- Master unreachable from Shadow (network/firewall)
- Cert distrust
- Version mismatch

### Shadow doesn't take over
- Shadow itself has issue (disk full, service crashed)
- Master → BTP tunnel intact but backend not, shadow can't help

### Split-brain (both active)
Rare. Should be prevented by SCC logic. If detected:
1. Manually stop one
2. Force role from remaining

## Backup config
**Configuration → Export** → download ZIP (encrypted).

Backup both Master and Shadow independently.

## Cost
Doubles hardware cost. Some orgs use single SCC + operational readiness to restore quickly (RTO ~1h).

HA justifiable for:
- Business-critical integrations
- 24/7 apps
- Regulatory requirements

title: SAP Cloud Connector: audit log y monitoring
excerpt: Ver logs de acceso, audit y traces del SCC.
body:
## Access log (por default)
SCC logs every call que pasa por el tunnel.

### Ver via UI
SCC UI → **Log And Trace Files** → **Access Log**

### Columnas
- Timestamp
- User (BTP user si principal propagation)
- Backend virtual host
- Backend URL/path
- HTTP method (GET/POST/etc.)
- Response code (200, 401, 500)
- Response time (ms)
- Bytes

### Filter
- Time range
- User
- Virtual host
- HTTP method
- Status code

### Export
- CSV
- Filter por rango + download

## Audit log
Acciones administrativas (config changes):
- User login/logout
- Add/remove subaccount
- Add/remove system
- Add/remove resource
- Certificate updates
- HA role changes

### Ver
SCC UI → **Log And Trace Files** → **Audit Log**

## Tracing
Debug logs para issue-specific analysis:

### Habilitar
SCC UI → **Log And Trace Files** → **Trace Level**:
- **INFO** (default)
- **DEBUG** — detailed calls
- **TRACE** — max detail (heavy overhead)

Select subaccount + component + level.

### Ver
**Trace Files** → download latest.

Log en filesystem:
- Linux: `/opt/sap/scc/log/scc_daemon.log`, `subaccount_<id>.log`
- Windows: `%ProgramData%\SAP\SAP Cloud Connector\log\`

## Log rotation
- Files rotate at 10 MB (default)
- Retained 5 most recent (default)

### Config
SCC UI → **Configuration** → **Log And Trace**:
- Max file size
- Max files retained
- Rotation pattern

## Export logs to central SIEM
### Syslog forward
1. **Configuration → Log And Trace → Audit Log → Syslog**
2. Syslog server host + port + facility
3. Format: RFC3164, RFC5424, or LEEF

SCC pushes audit events via UDP/TCP syslog to central SIEM (Splunk, Sentinel, ELK).

### JSON output
SCC 2.15+ soporta JSON structured log:
- Easier parsing en Splunk / ELK / Loki

## Métricas
### CPU/RAM del proceso
SCC UI → **Configuration → CPU And Memory**:
- Real-time chart
- Java heap usage
- Threads count

### Métricas via JMX (avanzado)
JMX endpoint (con auth) para monitor externo:
- Prometheus JMX exporter
- Grafana dashboards

## Alertas
### UI configuration
SCC UI → **Configuration → Notifications**:
- **Certificate expiring**: threshold N días
- **Tunnel state change**: on connect/disconnect
- **HA state change**
- **Error rate**: X errores en Y minutos

Email destination single o distribution list.

## Backend availability check
SCC checks systems periodically. Configurable:

SCC UI → system → **Availability Check** enabled:
- Interval: 60s
- Timeout: 10s

Fallos → status red en dashboard + optional email alert.

## Correlation con BTP audit
BTP tiene su propio audit trail (subaccount → Security → Audit Logs).

Correlacionar via:
- Request ID (some services propagate)
- Timestamp precision (segundos)
- User email

## Retention
Access log: 7 días default, hasta 90.
Audit log: 90 días default, hasta 1 año.

Cambiar en **Configuration → Log Retention**.

## Common uses

### 'Por qué el user X ve 401 al conectar?'
1. Access log filter user X, status 401
2. Ver timestamp, request URL, response
3. Correlacionar con SCC log en detalle mismo timestamp
4. Puede ser: principal propagation failed, or resource not exposed

### 'Con qué frecuencia se llama la API?'
Access log stats → count por URL/mes → capacity planning.

### 'Auditoria: quién cambió la config?'
Audit log filter by user + action type.

## Delete logs
Manual limpieza:
- UI → **Log And Trace Files** → select old files → delete
- O tunelling script en OS filesystem

**Cuidado**: si régimen compliance (SOX, ISO 27001), retención mandatory.

title: SAP Cloud Connector: HTTP resources — Access Policies
tags: scc, resource, access policy, url, whitelist
excerpt: Configurar qué URLs específicos on-premise son accesibles desde BTP.
body:
## Contexto
Por sistema, listás recursos permitidos. Sin lista → nada accesible (whitelist model).

## Add resource
SCC UI → subaccount → **Cloud To On-Premise → Access Control** → select system → tab **Resources → Add**:

### Fields
- **URL Path**: `/sap/opu/odata/sap/API_BUSINESS_PARTNER/`
- **Description**: 'Business Partner OData'
- **Access Policy**:
  - **Path Only**: exact match (path exacto)
  - **Path And All Sub-Paths**: prefix match
  - **Path And Query**: exact path + specific query params
- **WebSocket Upgrade Allowed**: si aplica

## Ejemplos

### Whole OData service (recomendado)
- URL: `/sap/opu/odata/sap/`
- Access Policy: **Path And All Sub-Paths**

Allows any OData service under `/sap/opu/odata/sap/*`.

### Specific service only
- URL: `/sap/opu/odata/sap/API_BUSINESS_PARTNER/`
- Access Policy: **Path And All Sub-Paths**

Only this service accessible.

### Static file resource
- URL: `/img/logo.png`
- Access Policy: **Path Only**

Exact file only.

### API restringido por query
- URL: `/api/products?environment=prod`
- Access Policy: **Path And Query**

## Multiple resources per system
Un sistema puede tener 10+ resources:
- OData API 1
- OData API 2
- Static content
- WebDynpro app

Cada uno individual.

## Wildcard behavior
No full wildcards en URLs. Solo trailing (subpaths).

### Wrong
- `/sap/*/service/` — no funciona (wildcard mid-path)

### Right
- `/sap/` con **Path And All Sub-Paths** — funciona (covers everything under /sap/)

## HTTP methods
By default, all methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH) allowed.

### Restrict methods
Resource → tab **Advanced Settings**:
- ✓ GET only
- Uncheck POST/DELETE

Use case: read-only proxy for reporting apps.

## Headers filter
SCC puede filter headers específicos:
- **Allowed request headers**: list de headers pasables al backend
- **Allowed response headers**: list de headers backend puede devolver

Default: most standard headers allowed. Restringir en high-security envs.

## Test resource
Select resource → **Check Availability**:
- SCC does HEAD/GET request al backend
- Green: OK
- Red: unreachable or unauthorized

## Access log filter
Access log filter por resource → cuántas llamadas, cuáles usuarios.

## Bulk operations
SCC 2.14+ soporta:
- Export resources a CSV
- Import resources desde CSV
- Copy resources between systems (dev → prod)

### Export
Select system → **Export Resources** → downloads CSV.

### Import
Select system → **Import Resources** → upload CSV. SCC validates + adds.

## Common patterns

### Fiori launchpad backend
```
/sap/opu/odata/sap/                # OData services
/sap/bc/ui2/                       # Fiori launchpad
/sap/bc/ui5_ui5/                   # UI5 apps
/sap/bc/lrep/                      # UI5 flexibility
/sap/hana/                         # HANA apps (if applicable)
```

### RFC destinations
For RFC systems (protocol=RFC), no URL paths — instead **RFC function** whitelist:
- Tab **Function Modules → Add**
- List of allowed function module names

Ejemplo: `BAPI_BUPA_ADDRESS_GET` (read only). Deny `BAPI_BUPA_ADDRESS_DELETE`.

### LDAP resources
Protocol LDAP → **LDAP Search Filters** section:
- Base DN
- Filter pattern

## Autorización check en backend
SCC no valida auth del user — solo relay. El backend (ECC/S4) executes auth check:
- `S_TCODE`, `S_TABU_DIS`, business auth objects
- Con principal propagation: user real
- Sin: technical user (all-or-nothing)

## Debug 403 / access denied
Access log muestra:
- SCC allowed the call (matched whitelist)
- Backend denied (auth issue)

Si SCC blocks:
- Log muestra 'Resource not found in whitelist'
- Add resource + re-check

## Best practices
- Whitelist tightly — only what's needed
- Regular audit — remove unused resources
- Log analysis — identify unused resources → candidates for removal
- Backup config antes de major changes

title: SAP Cloud Connector: RFC exposé — function whitelist
excerpt: Configurar RFC systems y whitelistear function modules específicas.
body:
## Contexto
Para systems tipo **ABAP System** con protocolo **RFC**, en vez de URL paths configurás **function module names** whitelist.

## Add RFC system
SCC UI → subaccount → **Cloud To On-Premise** → **Add**:
- **Backend Type**: ABAP System
- **Protocol**: RFC (o RFC over SNC)
- **Internal host**: `sapecc.empresa.local`
- **Instance number**: `00`
- **Client**: `100` (default)
- **Virtual host**: `virtual-ecc`
- **Virtual instance**: `00`
- **Principal Type**: X.509 or None

## Add function modules (resources)
Select system → **Resources** tab → **Add**:

### Modes
- **Standard**: exact match (e.g., `BAPI_BUPA_ADDRESS_GET`)
- **Prefix**: match by prefix (e.g., `BAPI_BUPA_*`)

### Regex-like patterns
```
BAPI_BUPA_ADDRESS_GET     # exact match
BAPI_BUPA_*               # prefix match, allows BAPI_BUPA_CREATE, GET, DELETE
BAPI_*                    # all BAPIs (broad, avoid en prod)
*                         # everything (never in prod)
```

## Ejemplo config
### Read-only Business Partner integration
```
BAPI_BUPA_ADDRESS_GETDETAIL
BAPI_BUPA_CONTACT_GETLIST
BAPI_BUPA_ROLES_GET
BAPI_BUPA_TAX_GET
BAPI_BUPA_ADDRESS_GET_ALL
```

### Full CRUD
```
BAPI_BUPA_ADDRESS_GETDETAIL
BAPI_BUPA_CREATE_FROM_DATA
BAPI_BUPA_ADDRESS_CHANGE
BAPI_BUPA_ADDRESS_REMOVE
BAPI_TRANSACTION_COMMIT   # required for commit
BAPI_TRANSACTION_ROLLBACK
```

## Common BAPIs
- **BAPI_MATERIAL_GET_DETAIL** — material master
- **BAPI_PO_GETDETAIL** — purchase order
- **BAPI_SALESORDER_CREATEFROMDAT2** — create sales order
- **BAPI_INCOMINGINVOICE_CREATE** — invoice receipt
- **BAPI_GOODSMVT_CREATE** — goods movement
- **RFC_READ_TABLE** — read any table (**PELIGRO** — no whitelist without careful thought)
- **BAPI_TRANSACTION_COMMIT** — commit changes (needed for BAPIs)

## Common patterns

### Read-only integration
Only `_GET`, `_READ`, `_LIST` functions. No commit needed for read.

### Transactional integration
Include `BAPI_TRANSACTION_COMMIT` and `BAPI_TRANSACTION_ROLLBACK`. BAPIs typically require these for changes to persist.

## Destination BTP config para RFC
```
Name: MY_ECC_RFC
URL: rfc://virtual-ecc:00 (virtual)
Type: RFC
Proxy Type: OnPremise
Authentication: BasicAuthentication or PrincipalPropagation
User: RFCUSER
Password: ****
sapclient: 100
sysnr: 00
```

## Uso desde app (Node.js SAP Cloud SDK)
```javascript
const { executeAsRfc } = require('@sap-cloud-sdk/connectivity');

const result = await executeRfc({
  destination: 'MY_ECC_RFC',
  functionName: 'BAPI_MATERIAL_GET_DETAIL',
  input: {
    MATERIAL: '000000000000000123',
    PLANT: '1000'
  }
});
console.log(result.MATERIAL_GENERAL);
```

## Debug de RFC call

### SCC log
Access log → filter RFC → ver function called + result.

### ECC side
- `SM59` no direct show — inbound RFC comes as pre-defined 'GATEWAY' style
- `SMGW` — gateway monitor sees active RFC connections
- User activity → `SM04` shows user with 'RFC' session

### Trace
- SCC subaccount log level DEBUG
- ECC user with ST01 authorization trace

## Errores comunes

### 'Function XXX not in whitelist'
SCC blocks the call. Add function to Resources.

### 'Access denied for user'
RFC user en ECC no tiene auth for the FM:
- `S_RFC` object with FMD_MODULE_NAME = the FM name
- Fix en PFCG del user

### 'Program not registered'
RFC destination points to registered TP that's not registered anymore. Verify SMGW.

### 'Connection error'
- Firewall between SCC and ECC blocks RFC port (3300 for instance 00)
- Wrong instance number in system config

## Security best practices
- **Never whitelist `*`** — allows all BAPIs
- **RFC_READ_TABLE** should NOT be exposed (allows arbitrary reads)
- **BAPI_USER_CREATE1** should be tightly controlled
- Prefer **narrow whitelist** — only functions you actively use
- **Audit annually** — remove unused whitelists

## RFC over SNC (secure)
For SNC-encrypted RFC:
- Backend needs SNC enabled
- SCC config: protocol **RFC over SNC**
- Config SNC name + libs

More secure than plain RFC. Recommended for production.

title: SAP Cloud Connector: LDAP integration
excerpt: Exponer LDAP/AD interno a apps BTP.
body:
## Uso
App en BTP necesita:
- Ver membership de grupos AD
- Query users por email/username
- Validar credentials contra AD

SCC hace de proxy LDAP outbound seguro.

## Add LDAP system
SCC UI → subaccount → **Cloud To On-Premise → Access Control → Add**:
- **Backend Type**: **LDAP Server**
- **Protocol**: **LDAP** o **LDAPS**
- **Internal host**: `ad-dc.empresa.local`
- **Internal port**: `389` (LDAP) o `636` (LDAPS)
- **Virtual host**: `virtual-ldap`
- **Virtual port**: `389`

## Add LDAP resources (search filters)
Select system → **Resources** tab.

### Structure de un LDAP resource
- **Base DN**: `OU=Users,DC=empresa,DC=local`
- **Filter**: `(objectClass=user)`
- **Scope**: `base`, `onelevel`, `subtree`

### Ejemplo: user search
- Base DN: `OU=Users,DC=empresa,DC=local`
- Filter: `(&(objectClass=user)(mail=*))`
- Scope: `subtree`

### Ejemplo: group membership
- Base DN: `OU=Groups,DC=empresa,DC=local`
- Filter: `(objectClass=group)`
- Scope: `subtree`

## Denegar contenido sensible
Restrict subtree DNs — don't allow all `DC=empresa,DC=local`:
- Instead specific OUs like `OU=Users`, `OU=Groups`
- Prevent enumeration de otros objects

## LDAPS con self-signed CA
Si el AD tiene cert self-signed:
1. SCC UI → **Configuration** → **On Premise** → **Trusted CA certificates for TLS Client**
2. Import the CA of your AD
3. LDAPS trust established

## Destination BTP
```
Name: MY_LDAP_DEST
Type: HTTP (o LDAP direct depending on library used)
URL: ldap://virtual-ldap:389
Proxy Type: OnPremise
Authentication: BasicAuthentication
User: cn=ldap_bind,ou=service,dc=empresa,dc=local
Password: ****
```

SAP Java Buildpack + Java LDAP libs, or Node LDAP client.

## Uso desde app Node.js
```javascript
const ldap = require('ldapjs');

const client = ldap.createClient({
  url: destinationUrl,
  proxy: proxyConfig  // SCC proxy
});

client.bind('cn=ldap_bind,ou=service,dc=empresa,dc=local', 'password', err => {
  if (err) return console.error(err);
  
  client.search('OU=Users,DC=empresa,DC=local', {
    filter: '(mail=jperez@empresa.com)',
    scope: 'sub'
  }, (err, res) => {
    res.on('searchEntry', entry => console.log(entry.object));
  });
});
```

## Common uses

### User validation flow
App BTP recibe login → app calls SCC → LDAP validates against AD → app grants/denies access.

### Group-based authorization
App BTP retrieves user's group memberships from AD → maps to app roles.

### User info sync
BTP directory synced from AD via SCC — user details available in BTP without duplicate data entry.

## Errores comunes

### 'Bind DN unknown'
Wrong service account DN. Verify DN in AD:
```powershell
Get-ADUser -Identity ldap_bind | Select DistinguishedName
```

### 'Insufficient access rights'
Service account no tiene permission a leer objects requested. Grant read en those OUs.

### 'Referral chase failed'
AD forest con multiples domains → referrals. SCC LDAP client may need config to chase referrals:
- Depends on library used from BTP app

### 'Cert not trusted' (LDAPS)
CA of AD cert missing en SCC trust store. Import CA.

## Security

### Service account principle of least privilege
- Read-only rights
- Only on required OUs
- Long complex password
- Rotate quarterly

### Encryption in transit
- **Prefer LDAPS** (636) over LDAP (389)
- Or LDAP with STARTTLS

### Logging
- SCC access log captures each search
- AD-side: enable AD DS audit for readings if sensitive

## Alternative: SCIM API
SAP BTP prefers **SCIM 2.0** modern API for user provisioning:
- If your on-prem has SCIM endpoint, use HTTP protocol instead of LDAP
- More RESTful, easier to work with

LDAP still relevant for legacy integrations.

title: SAP Cloud Connector: HANA DB exposure
excerpt: Exponer HANA on-premise para apps BTP que necesitan JDBC access directo.
body:
## Contexto
App BTP consumes HANA de dos maneras:
1. **Via OData/HTTP** (recomendado) — HANA XSA services
2. **JDBC direct** — apps que necesitan raw SQL, migration tools, reporting BI

Option 1 usa protocol HTTP en SCC.
Option 2 usa protocol **TCP** en SCC.

## Add HANA system
SCC UI → subaccount → **Cloud To On-Premise → Add**:

### Config
- **Backend Type**: **Non-SAP System**
- **Protocol**: **TCP** (para JDBC access)
- **Internal host**: `hana.empresa.local`
- **Internal port**: `30015` (HANA MDC tenant, o 39013 for system)
- **Virtual host**: `virtual-hana`
- **Virtual port**: `30015`

### Ports HANA typical
- **3<inst>13** — System DB
- **3<inst>15** — Tenant DB
- **3<inst>17** — Multi-tenant

Donde `<inst>` es el instance number (usually 00 = 30015).

## Destination BTP
```
Name: MY_HANA_DEST
Type: JDBC (o custom depending on app)
URL: jdbc:sap://virtual-hana:30015/?databaseName=<tenant>
Proxy Type: OnPremise
User: DBADMIN (o service account)
Password: ****
```

## Uso desde Java app
```java
DataSource ds = ... // SAP Cloud SDK provides
Connection conn = ds.getConnection();
Statement stmt = conn.createStatement();
ResultSet rs = stmt.executeQuery("SELECT * FROM SCHEMA.TABLE");
```

## Uso desde Node.js
```javascript
const hana = require('@sap/hana-client');
const conn = hana.createConnection();
conn.connect({
  serverNode: 'virtual-hana:30015',
  uid: 'DBUSER',
  pwd: 'password',
  // SCC proxy config via SDK
});
```

## Auth options

### Basic (user + password)
- Simple
- Password rotation manual

### Kerberos SSO (con SNC)
- User BTP → same Kerberos ticket → HANA
- Requires domain trust

### X.509 Certificate
- SAP proprietary
- Best for cloud-native scenarios

## Ver connections HANA
In HANA cockpit:
- **System Overview → Connections** → active sessions
- Filter por user o app name

## Common issues

### 'Cannot open TCP connection'
- Port not open en firewall (SCC → HANA)
- HANA service not listening on that port
- Test: `telnet hana.empresa.local 30015` from SCC server

### 'Authentication failed'
- User doesn't exist en HANA
- Password expired
- User locked por too many failed attempts

### 'Access denied on schema/table'
- User doesn't have SELECT on the schema
- Grant en HANA:
```sql
GRANT SELECT ON SCHEMA MY_SCHEMA TO 'MY_USER';
```

## Performance
### JDBC over SCC tunnel = latency added
- Every query round-trip through SCC + tunnel
- Batch operations preferred over row-by-row
- Prepared statements

### Not for high-frequency small queries
If app needs 10,000 small queries/sec — reconsider architecture. Move data to BTP-side HANA or use OData for aggregations.

## Alternative: HANA Cloud replication
Atractivo:
- Replicate on-prem HANA data to HANA Cloud
- Apps in BTP query the local (cloud) HANA — fast
- Eventual consistency with on-prem

Products: SAP Data Provisioning, SLT (System Landscape Transformation), Smart Data Integration (SDI).

## SSL/TLS
HANA encryption in transit:
- **encrypt=true** in JDBC URL
- **trustCert=true** or specify CA

```
jdbc:sap://virtual-hana:30015/?databaseName=X&encrypt=true&validateCertificate=false
```

### Cert chain
SCC forwards TCP as-is, cert validation happens at HANA client end.

If HANA cert self-signed:
- Import HANA cert to Java trust store (JKS) of the app

## Access log
SCC logs the TCP connection (bytes in/out), but not the SQL content (TCP is opaque).

For SQL-level audit, use HANA audit trail:
```sql
CREATE AUDIT POLICY 'AllReads' AUDITING SUCCESS SELECT ON MY_SCHEMA.MY_TABLE LEVEL INFO;
ALTER AUDIT POLICY 'AllReads' ENABLE;
```

## Bandwidth
Data-heavy apps → measure bandwidth SCC-to-BTP.
Large query results transferred over tunnel.

For bulk data movement: consider export files, cloud-native ETL tools.

## Best practices
- Use **least privilege** HANA users
- **Rotate passwords** periodically
- Prefer **HTTP/OData** if possible; TCP is more restrictive
- **Monitor query performance** via HANA cockpit
- **Audit SQL access** for compliance

title: SAP Cloud Connector: backup y restore de config
excerpt: Export/import config del SCC (para migrations, backups, DR).
body:
## Uso backup
SCC config guarda:
- Subaccount definitions
- Systems
- Resources
- Certificates
- Auth mapping rules
- HA config

Backup regular es crítico. Perdiste config = re-hacer todo desde cero (horas/días de trabajo).

## Export via UI
SCC UI → **Configuration → Configuration** → **Export All**:
1. Enter passphrase para encrypt export
2. Download ZIP file

### Contents del ZIP
- Config JSON files (encrypted)
- Private keys (encrypted)
- Certificates

## Filesystem backup
Alternative: backup directorio config completo.

### Linux
```bash
sudo systemctl stop scc_daemon
sudo tar -czf scc-backup-$(date +%F).tgz /opt/sap/scc/config /opt/sap/scc/state
sudo systemctl start scc_daemon
```

### Windows
```powershell
Stop-Service 'SAP Cloud Connector 2.0'
Compress-Archive -Path 'C:\ProgramData\SAP\SAP Cloud Connector\configuration' -DestinationPath 'C:\backups\scc-config-$(Get-Date -Format yyyy-MM-dd).zip'
Start-Service 'SAP Cloud Connector 2.0'
```

**Encrypted at rest** — the config uses SCC's master key. Backup includes it (or use exported passphrase).

## Import (restore)
SCC UI → **Configuration → Configuration** → **Import**:
1. Upload the exported ZIP
2. Enter the passphrase used at export
3. Confirm — overrides current config

**Warning**: import wipes current config. Use in fresh install or intentional replace.

### Merge import
Selectively import only certain subaccounts/systems:
- Advanced import options in UI

## Migration scenario
### Move SCC from Server A to Server B
1. On Server A: **Export** config (encrypted ZIP)
2. Install fresh SCC on Server B (same version!)
3. On Server B: **Import** the ZIP
4. Verify:
   - Tunnels reconnect
   - Systems test OK
   - Resources accessible
5. Decommission Server A

### Version upgrade + migration
1. Upgrade Server A to latest SCC version
2. Verify current config still works
3. Export from A (v2.16)
4. Install SCC v2.16 on Server B
5. Import config
6. Test
7. DNS/traffic switch to B

## Automated backup
### Cron job (Linux)
```bash
# /etc/cron.d/scc-backup
0 2 * * * root /usr/local/bin/scc-backup.sh
```

```bash
# /usr/local/bin/scc-backup.sh
#!/bin/bash
BACKUP_DIR=/backups/scc
DATE=$(date +%F)
mkdir -p $BACKUP_DIR
tar -czf $BACKUP_DIR/scc-$DATE.tgz /opt/sap/scc/config /opt/sap/scc/state
# Remove backups older than 30 days
find $BACKUP_DIR -name 'scc-*.tgz' -mtime +30 -delete
```

### Task Scheduler (Windows)
PowerShell script triggered daily via Task Scheduler.

## Test restore quarterly
Backups useless si nunca probaste el restore.

1. Setup test SCC en VM
2. Import backup
3. Verify config, connectivity, resource access
4. Document any issues
5. Update runbook

## Config version control (Git)
Advanced: export config regularly and commit to Git.

```bash
cd /opt/scc-config-repo
scp scc:/backups/scc/latest.tgz .
git add . && git commit -m "SCC config $(date)"
git push
```

Advantages:
- Diff between versions
- Rollback to specific date
- Audit trail

**But**: contents encrypted (opaque to Git diff). Alternative: export in plain text (JSON) via API, less secure.

## Backup encryption key rotation
SCC master key can be rotated:
1. UI → **Configuration → Encryption**
2. Generate new key
3. Old backups: still decryptable with old passphrase
4. New backups: encrypted with new key

Document key generation dates. Retain old keys en secure vault to decrypt older backups if needed.

## HA backup considerations
Master/Shadow — backup both, or just master?

Master syncs to Shadow, so Master's config is authoritative. **Backup only Master** suffice.

But Shadow-side certs may differ (per-instance). Full DR restore may require both.

## Common backup pitfalls

### 'Config too large'
SCC config can be > 10 MB with many systems. Test import in staging first.

### Passphrase lost
Without passphrase, ZIP is unrecoverable. Store passphrase in enterprise password vault.

### Wrong version import
Don't import config from newer SCC into older SCC. May silently fail or corrupt.

## Recovery time
- Full SCC install + config import: 30-60 min
- Test post-restore: 1-2 hours
- Total RTO: 2-3 hours realistic

For faster: HA setup — Shadow takes over automatic in <1 min.

title: SAP Cloud Connector: proxy corporativo
tags: scc, proxy, http proxy, corporate, outbound
excerpt: Configurar SCC detrás de un proxy HTTP corporativo para llegar a BTP.
body:
## Contexto
Empresas restringen tráfico saliente por proxy (Squid, Zscaler, BlueCoat). SCC necesita config específica para atravesar.

## Config UI
SCC UI → **Configuration → HTTPS Proxy**:
- **Enable HTTPS Proxy for Communication**: ✓
- **Proxy Host**: `proxy.empresa.local`
- **Proxy Port**: `8080`
- **Non-Proxy Hosts** (bypass list): `localhost, 127.0.0.1, *.empresa.local`
- **Authentication** (if proxy needs auth):
  - **Type**: None / Basic / Kerberos / NTLM
  - **User** / **Password**

Save.

## No-proxy hosts
Wildcard soporte:
- `*.empresa.local` — cualquier subdomain interno
- `10.0.0.0/8` — no soportado directamente; use lista de hosts
- Comma-separated

## Basic auth
Simple user/pass. Contraseña encrypted en config.

### Kerberos SSO
Proxy con SSO Kerberos:
- Requires SPN registered for SCC (may need service account with SPN)
- Configure Java Kerberos config file (`krb5.conf`) on SCC server

### NTLM
Proxy con Windows integrated auth:
- Configure user account with NTLM cred
- Java NTLM library used by SCC

## Testing proxy
UI → **Test Proxy** button → SCC does outbound call via proxy → verifies.

### Failure modes

#### 'Proxy timeout'
- Proxy host DNS resolution failed
- Proxy port blocked in local firewall
- Proxy service down

#### 'Proxy authentication required'
- Wrong credentials
- Auth type mismatch (proxy needs Kerberos, config says Basic)

#### 'Certificate error'
- Proxy does SSL inspection (MITM cert)
- Import proxy's CA cert in SCC trust store:
  - **Configuration → Trust Store** → import CA cert

## Bypass proxy for specific targets
Some large orgs have direct routes to Azure/AWS regions. SCC can bypass proxy for BTP endpoints:

- Non-proxy hosts: `cf.eu10.hana.ondemand.com, connectivitynotification.cf.eu10.hana.ondemand.com`

Direct connection faster, but requires firewall rules to allow it.

## Configuring per subaccount
Multiple subaccounts might use different proxies:
- SCC UI → **Configuration → HTTPS Proxy** — global default
- Override per subaccount → subaccount → **Advanced Settings**

Rare but possible: some subaccounts via proxy, others direct.

## Bandwidth consumed by proxy
Proxy might have rate limits per source IP (SCC's IP).

Monitor via proxy admin. Whitelist SCC IP if needed.

## Common corporate policies
### SSL inspection (MITM)
Proxy decrypts HTTPS traffic, inspects, re-encrypts with proxy's own cert.

SCC needs to trust the proxy CA:
- Get CA cert from InfoSec
- Import to SCC trust store

### Content filtering
Proxy may block certain URLs. Whitelist SAP domains:
- `*.hana.ondemand.com`
- `*.cfapps.eu10.hana.ondemand.com`

### DLP (Data Loss Prevention)
Proxies may block outgoing data patterns (PII, credit cards).

SCC traffic includes payloads to BTP. Coordinate with security to avoid false positives.

## Direct outbound (recommended if possible)
If compliance allows: firewall rule for SCC IP → outbound 443 direct (no proxy):
- Simpler troubleshooting
- Better performance
- Fewer moving parts

## Fallback / redundancy
Some enterprises have failover proxies. SCC only supports 1 proxy at a time.

If primary proxy down: manual switch to backup proxy config, or use load balancer VIP.

## Debug proxy issues
### SCC log
- Level DEBUG on `com.sap.core.connectivity.proxy`
- Look for connection attempts, timeouts, auth challenges

### Network capture (tcpdump/Wireshark)
- Confirm TCP handshake to proxy host
- Confirm HTTPS CONNECT tunnel established

### Test with curl (same server)
```bash
curl -x http://proxy.empresa.local:8080 -U user:pass https://cf.eu10.hana.ondemand.com
```

If curl works, SCC should. If not, network/proxy issue.

## Perf tuning
### Proxy latency
Every request adds latency:
- SCC → proxy → BTP

Optimize by ensuring proxy is on the same network segment as SCC (low RTT).

### Keep-alive
SCC uses persistent connections. Proxy must support keep-alive for optimal performance.

Some proxies terminate long-lived connections → SCC re-establishes → adds overhead.

## Autorización
Proxy service account for SCC:
- Least privilege
- Only allow outbound to `*.hana.ondemand.com` if strict
- Rotate password quarterly
- Log all auth events for audit
